1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.

3.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

4.meaning: 'Bow down!' — the command form of rakaʿa, to bow, to bend the body at the waist; the word that names the rukūʿ, the bowing posture of the ritual prayer, and more broadly humble submission.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The initial i- is only a helping vowel added so the command can be pronounced; the core is rkaʿ 'bow!'. The -ū ending addresses a masculine plural: 'you all, bow!' — the plural command ending regularly used when a group is ordered to act.

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: 'They bow' / 'they are bowing' — bending the upper body forward from the waist, above all the bow of the ritual prayer (rukūʿ). The root carries the wider sense of lowering oneself in humility and submission, so the word implies reverent self-abasement, not merely a physical stoop.

parts.en: masculine plural subject 'they', with -na marking a plain statement

6.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, Form I (the plain, unaugmented form of the root). The ya- prefix makes the doer third person masculine, and the -ū of the ending makes that subject a masculine plural 'they'. The final -na is the indicative marker, signalling a plain factual statement — 'they bow / they are bowing / they will bow'. That -na drops away whenever a particle puts the verb into the subjunctive or jussive (as in 'they will not bow' or 'they did not bow'), so its presence shows the verb stands free of any such particle.
6.root: ر-ك-ع (r-k-ʿ) — to bow, bend low; humble submission

1.meaning: Woe — an exclamation of severe warning, condemnation, or lamentation; used to express doom and destruction upon someone.
1.grammar: A noun (in the nominative case, marked by tanwīn -un) used as an exclamation of condemnation. It is indeclinable in some usages but here carries the nominative indefinite marker. 'Waylun li-' means 'woe to [someone].'
1.root: و-ي-ل (w-y-l) — destruction, ruin, woe (no productive verb in Classical Arabic)

2.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
2.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

3.meaning: To the deniers / beliers — those who persistently deny the truth; woe is proclaimed against them.

parts.en: accusative/genitive ending of sound masculine plural

3.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil) of the Form II verb kadhdhaba (to deny, to call a liar), in the definite sound masculine plural, genitive case after the preposition li-. The Form II intensifies the action: mukadhdhibūn = persistent, deliberate deniers.
3.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to deny; كَذَّبَ = to persistently deny; مُكَذِّب = one who denies

1.meaning: So in/by which …? — a compound of 'so/then', the preposition 'in/by', and the interrogative 'which/what'. It opens a question asking 'in which?' or 'by what?', expecting a specific item to be identified.
1.grammar: A particle cluster: 'fa-' links to what precedes ('so/then'); 'bi-' is the preposition 'in/by/with'. The interrogative 'ayy' carries the -i ending because it is genitive, the case required after a preposition. It questions which one of a class is meant, and normally precedes a following noun ('which … ?').
1.root: — (particles + interrogative)

2.meaning: Speech, talk, or an account; a piece of discourse or report — that which is newly spoken or related.
2.grammar: An indefinite singular noun ('a talk / a report'). The -in ending is genitive with nunation (the -n marking 'a/an'), the form taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …').
2.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to be new, to happen; to relate, to speak

3.meaning: After it / afterward — the time-or-place word 'after' joined to the pronoun 'it/him'. It marks what follows something else in sequence, whether in time, rank, or position.
3.grammar: An adverb of time/place, 'after', which is fixed in the -a form (the accusative used for such adverbs). The attached pronoun 'it/him' takes the -hu shape because it follows that -a vowel. Together: 'after it/him'.
3.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow; afterness in time or place

4.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.
